clue.text: Sound content about hunt for customer

indicators.note: the purr is wrapped about the hunt, its letters sitting either side

parts.note: a cat's purr is the sound it makes when content
to hunt is to chase

explanation.surface: A contented noise surrounds the search for a buyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound content' looks like 'satisfied noise' in general; it is the cat's PURR, opened up by 'about' to hold CHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer in a shop is its customer; synonym.

clue.text: Part of film about black revolutionary

indicators.note: the reel goes round the black, holding it inside

parts.note: a reel is one spool, a portion, of a film
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A section of a movie concerns a Black insurgent.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent who rises against authority is a revolutionary; synonym.

clue.text: Engineers were effective turning round river

indicators.note: the engineers and the effective verb are read backwards together

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
brakes or a policy 'bit' when they took effect

explanation.surface: Engineers succeeded in diverting a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were effective' is BIT, as in 'the new rules bit'; RE plus BIT read backwards gives the Roman river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tiber is the river flowing through Rome; example.

clue.text: Snarls as gentle knight is wounded

indicators.note: a wounded thing is damaged and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A mild-mannered knight snarls in pain on being wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wounded' rearranges AS, GENTLE and N; 'Snarls' is a verb meaning tangles, not growls.
explanation.definitionFit: To snarl string or hair is to tangle it up in knots; synonym.

clue.text: Queen briefly embraced by sister, a tiny thing

indicators.note: the queen's short name is hugged by the sister, sitting inside her

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
Cleo is the short form of Cleopatra, queen of Egypt

explanation.surface: A queen, for a moment, is hugged by her sister, a small figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen briefly' is CLEO, a shortening of Cleopatra, not a cut-down QUEEN or ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton or neutron in an atom's nucleus is a minuscule particle; description.

clue.text: I lead the congregation, in short? That's laying it on thick

indicators.note: cut short, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: said by a minister: I'm pastor

explanation.surface: A vicar's boast prompts the retort that he's overdoing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The speaker says I'M PASTOR; 'in short' clips its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is the painting technique of applying pigment thickly to the canvas; descriptive definition.

clue.text: Allow flesh to form a hard mass? Cynical remark

parts.note: to let is to allow
flesh as food is the meat
to cake is to harden into a crust, as mud does

explanation.surface: A cook's instruction to let the joint harden becomes a sneering comment.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase attributed to Marie Antoinette is read literally as letting meat harden.
explanation.definitionFit: The supposed royal reply to starving peasants is the classic example of callous dismissiveness.

clue.text: People of remarkably elitist leaning?

indicators.note: in a remarkable, unusual way, so the two words' letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a snobbish class of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the intellectual class is often seen as elitist.
explanation.definitionFit: The intellectual elite of a society are often accused of looking down on others; description.

clue.text: Problems are over for Darwin

indicators.note: turned over, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: sums are arithmetic problems

explanation.surface: Charles Darwin's difficulties have come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darwin' misleads towards Charles; it is his grandfather Erasmus Darwin.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus Darwin was a physician and poet, grandfather of the naturalist; first name of a famous bearer.

clue.text: A twist for animal in the case

indicators.note: the reversed animal goes inside the word 'the'
a twist applied to the animal turns its letters backwards

parts.note: a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A twisty puzzle features an animal as part of the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' looks like filler but is the container; 'twist for' turns the animal round before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is short for an attaché case, a slim briefcase for documents.

clue.text: Quickly cooked one thrown in raw after first being prepared

indicators.note: the raw part comes after the prepared word
made ready, so the letters of 'first' are rearranged
the one is tossed into the raw word

parts.note: raw meat or skin is red
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Something cooked fast after first being prepared from raw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being prepared' rearranges FIRST to STIRF; 'thrown in' puts I into RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-frying is a quick method of cooking in a hot wok, tossing the food constantly.

clue.text: Pair of birds, perhaps, cold in the hillside

indicators.note: the cold letter sits within the hillside

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish word for a hillside
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Two game birds shiver on a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: BRAE is Scots for a hillside or bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Two pheasants or partridges shot are a brace; game-shooting term, 'perhaps' because other things come in braces.

clue.text: Punches perhaps thrown here in area of the kidneys — that's out of line

indicators.note: the line letter is left out of the kidney adjective

parts.note: renal means relating to the kidneys

explanation.surface: A boxer's low blow to the kidneys is out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punches thrown in area of the kidneys' suggests a foul; 'out of line' drops L from RENAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing bout takes place in a venue where blows are traded; example.

clue.text: Rumour of fruit and what it becomes in French and English

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
grapes become wine, which in French is vin

explanation.surface: Gossip about a fruit and its transformation in two languages.
explanation.walkthrough: VIN is French for wine, what grapes become.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something 'on the grapevine' means by informal word of mouth; idiom.

clue.text: Obviously with resignation one has to go

indicators.note: the one must leave, so it is removed from the longer word

parts.note: patiently means with calm acceptance or resignation
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Clearly, after resigning, someone has to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resignation' suggests quitting a job; here it is patient acceptance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done clearly, plain for all to see, is done openly; synonym.

clue.text: Fiddle restaurant expenses, being extremely careful to have only a starter in each

indicators.note: only the first letter, a starter, of each of the words is kept

explanation.surface: Padding a restaurant bill while carefully ordering only starters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like cheating on expenses; it is the noun, an old bowed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebec is a medieval stringed instrument played with a bow, a forerunner of the violin.

clue.text: Small garden supports heroin? That's said to be lucky

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting pieces sit underneath the drug

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
to hoe is to garden, weeding the soil

explanation.surface: A little garden is a front for drugs, said to be good fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supports' puts S and HOE below HORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm.

clue.text: Bone in breast or back, I'm not sure

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship
um is a hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Is the bone in the chest or the back? Someone hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone is the flat bone at the front of the chest; anatomical synonym.

clue.text: Filled with sulphur, one that collects light wine

indicators.note: the light-collecting organ is filled with the sulphur letter, holding it inside

parts.note: the retina is the light-sensitive layer of the eye
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A sulphurous light-collector is a cheap white.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white flavoured with pine resin; example.

clue.text: Quickly create wordplay that's raised after sport

indicators.note: the raised pun comes after the sport

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: lifted up in a down answer, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a pun is wordplay

explanation.surface: Knocking up a joke after a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' works only in a down answer, where reading upwards reverses the word; to run up a dress is to make it quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something up, like curtains, is to make it fast; phrasal verb.

clue.text: Villain's evil son breaking into vehicles

definitions.note: read as 'villain is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: the evil and son pieces burst into the vehicles

parts.note: bikes are vehicles
ill can mean evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: A wicked son breaks into cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the brutal burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Sikes is the murderous criminal of Oliver Twist; literary example.

clue.text: City snobs, ill-mannered, spinning bottles

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters held are read backwards
the words bottle up, contain, the answer's letters

explanation.surface: Rude city snobs spin bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-mannered' looks like an anagram signal; the letters sit backwards inside 'snobs, ill'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal; example.

clue.text: Not confident local, not having opened, has laid wine on

indicators.note: in a down answer the local word has the wine laid on top of it

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: without its opening letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a native is a local person

explanation.surface: An unsure local has not opened the wine he's laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a pub; it is a NATIVE, losing its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hesitant, uncertain approach is a tentative one; synonym.

clue.text: Two firms taking in new officer

indicators.note: the two firms absorb the new letter inside them

parts.note: CO is a company, a firm; stable also means firm

explanation.surface: Two companies merge and take on a new police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firms' is used two ways: CO the business, STABLE the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A constable is the lowest-ranked police officer in Britain; example.

clue.text: With which one looks helpless?

parts.note: naked can mean defenceless, so an unaided eye looks unprotected

explanation.surface: What makes someone appear helpless?
explanation.walkthrough: Seeing without a telescope is looking with something defenceless.
explanation.definitionFit: The unaided eye is what you look with when no lens or telescope helps; descriptive pun.

clue.text: Durable, as batsman number eleven is good

parts.note: the number eleven batsman in cricket is the last man in

explanation.surface: A tail-end batsman is praised for staying power.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the eleventh batsman is the last man in to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something long-lasting endures; synonym.

clue.text: Four-figure sum given to virtually crazy old woman

indicators.note: the trimmed crazy word is added to the sum

parts.note: a grand is a thousand, a four-figure amount

indicators.note: almost all of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A thousand pounds handed to a nearly mad old lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother is affectionately an older woman of the family; 'old woman' as relative.

clue.text: Small boy's poking damaged ear, somewhere near canal

indicators.note: the boy's possessive pokes into the rearranged ear
a damaged ear is broken up, so its letters are reordered

parts.note: Ed is a short boy's name, so Ed's

explanation.surface: A little boy pokes his injured ear, not far from the canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canal' sounds anatomical next to 'ear'; it is the Suez Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Sea lies at the southern end of the Suez Canal; location.

clue.text: First to make a decree that's cut off sinister group

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken
the decree is cut short, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a fiat is an official decree

explanation.surface: First issuing a decree, then a sinister group is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is a secret criminal organisation; example of a menacing gang.

clue.text: Some paint on one American native

parts.note: a coat is one layer of paint
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A daub of paint on an indigenous American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some paint' suggests a hidden word; it is a COAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a raccoon-like mammal native to the Americas; example.
